nodes.title: Import the template outlet for recursion
nodes.why: treeTpl renders one level and calls itself for each node's children through ngTemplateOutlet; FormsModule serves the two ngModel drafts, and @for and @if need no import.
nodes.alternative: Import CommonModule for the outlet, or move each comment into a child component that renders its own replies.
nodes.tradeoff: Importing NgTemplateOutlet alone keeps the dependency list exact and the state in one component; a recursive child component would isolate each comment's markup but need inputs and outputs for every action.

nodes.title: Hold the whole tree in one signal
nodes.why: Top-level comments and every nested reply live in this one array of nodes, so each add or reply is a single update, and the template starts its recursion from comments().
nodes.alternative: Keep a flat list of comments with a parentId on each and group the replies by parent while rendering.
nodes.tradeoff: A nested tree matches the rendering, but a deep insert must copy its path; a flat list turns every insert into an append and moves the work into grouping replies by parentId.

nodes.title: Store one active reply id
nodes.why: Only the comment whose id equals activeReplyId() shows the reply box, so opening a box on another comment closes the previous one without touching the tree.
nodes.alternative: Give every node an isReplying flag and reset the others whenever one opens.
nodes.tradeoff: One id cannot hold two open drafts, which this UI does not want; per-node flags could, but closing the rest would need a walk over the whole tree on every Reply click.

nodes.title: Put new top-level comments first
nodes.why: The spread builds a new array with the new comment at the front, so the signal sees a new value while every existing comment object keeps its identity for track comment.id.
nodes.alternative: Insert the comment in place at the front of the array that comments() returns.
nodes.tradeoff: The copy costs one array per new comment; an in-place insert avoids it but leaves the signal holding the same array, so nothing computed from comments() would see the change.

nodes.title: Store a new tree for every reply
nodes.why: submitReply passes the current tree to withReply and stores the result, so the signal receives a new root array and the branch with the new reply re-renders.
nodes.alternative: Find the parent with a findById search and push the reply into parent.children.
nodes.tradeoff: withReply is longer than a push; the push repaints only because the Post click marks the view, so a computed over the tree or a reply that arrives from a request would never see it.

nodes.title: Return untouched branches as they are
nodes.why: A branch without the parent gets its original children array back, so its node is returned unchanged and only the parent and its ancestors are copied with { ...node, children }.
nodes.alternative: Spread every node on the way down, rebuilding the whole tree for one reply.
nodes.tradeoff: The recursion still visits every node, but it allocates only along one path; copying everything is simpler to write but replaces objects that did not change.
